It was a wild round of European football defined by major upsets and tough tests for bookmakers and analytical tools alike. Surprise results like Brighton defeating Manchester City and Parma shocking Atalanta made for a challenging set of fixtures across the leagues.

Looking ahead, the model has not identified any upcoming outcomes with a high expected value of ten percent or more. Any slight differences between the model and Bet365 remain modest, making any potential divergences worth a closer look rather than taking them at face value.

Looking back at the completed matches, Bet365 generally maintained its historical edge in accuracy, but the model recorded some notable successes where it broke from the consensus. In Ligue 1, the model correctly called Lille to beat Lens with a 47.8% home win chance, whereas Bet365 had made Lens the 2.50 decimal odds favourite. The model also enjoyed a strong call in the Bundesliga, correctly tipping Werder Bremen over Hoffenheim with a 39.2% assessment while the bookmaker leaned toward Hoffenheim at 2.30 odds.

When favourites stumbled, however, the model paid a heavy price in its log loss accuracy score, where lower numbers indicate better performance. In Serie A, Milan's 3-1 derby triumph over Inter Milan proved expensive after the model assigned Inter a 61.9% away win chance. An even larger stumble came in Germany, where Elversberg's 4-1 rout of Mainz completely overturned the model's confident 76.0% away expectation. Over in the Premier League, the model fared much better on Bournemouth's 2-0 home win against Leeds, generating an impressive 0.544 log loss compared to Bet365's 0.796.
